brief: Bad vs Good vs Great cold emails — same intent, three radically different replies.

slots.body: Every cold email asks for the same thing: a conversation. Yet the response rate swings from silence to meetings. The gap is not the ask—it's the angle.
slots.note: Intent is constant. Framing changes everything.

slots.body: Hi [Name], I hope you are well. We are a leading provider of AI solutions. I would love to jump on a quick call to discuss your needs. Are you free Tuesday?
Hi [Name], noticed your team doubled headcount in Q2. Most fast-growing sales teams struggle with onboarding velocity. We cut ramp time by 30% for similar teams.
slots.note: Relevant hook, but still slightly self-serving.

slots.body: Hi [Name], saw your Series B announcement—congrats. I interviewed three VPs who scaled through similar rounds. Their biggest regret was delaying revops hires. Happy to send the notes.
slots.note: Leads with value. The meeting becomes a natural next step.

slots.body: Bad emails beg. Good emails pitch. Great emails teach. The reply rate skyrockets when the sender becomes a resource before they become a vendor.
slots.note: Flip the timeline: give, then ask.

slots.body: Before you send, delete every 'I' and 'we' until you have at least two 'you' or 'your' insights. If you cannot offer a micro-win, do not hit send.
slots.note: One genuine insight beats a hundred templates.

slots.body: Save this framework and rewrite your next cold email before lunch. Your future reply rate will thank you.
